commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Cast Admiral Brass, Unsinkable ({2}{U}{B}{R}); its ETB mills four. Fill the graveyard with Pirates (Entomb, Buried Alive, Ripples of Undeath's precombat mill, Mary Read and Anne Bonny, Malcolm, channel/discard), then every beginning of combat on our turn return a Pirate creature card as a hasty base-4/4 with a finality counter. Prefer Pirates whose ETB/attack triggers do work regardless of base stats (Hostage Taker, Amphin Mutineer, Coercive Recruiter, Kitesail Larcenist, Jhoira, Zara, Port Razer). Roaming Throne naming Pirate doubles the Brass trigger and the returned Pirates' triggers; Power Conduit removes finality counters at instant speed and Siren's Ruse resets a returned Pirate as a new object (CR 400.7), so Pirates can die and be reused; Port Razer and Timestream Navigator add combats/turns, each with another Brass trigger.
protected_core: Brass's Tunnel-Grinder // Tecutlan, the Searing Rift
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Power Bracket 4 — Optimized: six Game Changers (Ancient Tomb, Cyclonic Rift, Demonic Tutor, Fierce Guardianship, Jeska's Will, Vampiric Tutor), fast reanimation and tutors, but no deterministic two-card infinite identified; not cEDH.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Keep the list a Pirate-tribal graveyard-recursion deck: every add is a Pirate creature with ETB/attack value Brass can recur; reject generic reanimator payloads (Maskwood Nexus, non-Pirate fatties) and generic goodstuff (Rhystic-style taxes, Herald's Horn).

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps: Reviewed all 99 by quantity: baseline 34 physical lands in 31 rows (2x Island, 2x Mountain, 2x Swamp), candidate 33 (Crumbling Necropolis cut). Brass's Tunnel-Grinder is a front-face artifact (MV 3), not an opening-hand land drop, so it is not counted as a land. 8 mana rocks (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, 3 Signets, 3 Talismans); 30 Pirate/creature slots including Wonder; 8 graveyard/reanimation (Animate Dead, Buried Alive, Entomb, Faithless Looting -> Ripples of Undeath in candidate, Living Death, Patriarch's Bidding, Reanimate, Victimize); tutors/draw (Demonic, Vampiric, Jeska's Will, Kindred Discovery, Black Market Connections); 10 interaction/protection pieces; engines Power Conduit, Roaming Throne, Shared Animosity. Overlap: Treasure ramp is over-supplied by low-impact two-drops (Scallywag) while repeatable removal-on-ETB and extra-turn effects were under-supplied.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: CORRECTED REV2 (ChatGPT review item 1; quantity-counted from the rev2 Oracle snapshot). Baseline: 34 lands, 8 rocks = 42 mana permanents, plus Tunnel-Grinder and Treasure makers (Corsair Captain, Lannery Storm, Malcolm Navigator, Black Market Connections, Edward Kenway and others). Unrestricted colored land sources U21/B19/R18, plus Cavern of Souls / Exotic Orchard / Secluded Courtyard (conditional) for U24/B22/R21. Each color also has 5 rock sources. The rev1 memo's '31 lands' and '26/24/24' figures came from counting rows, not quantities, and are withdrawn. Candidate: 33 lands (Crumbling Necropolis cut), 8 rocks = 41; land sources U20/B18/R17 (23/21/20 with the conditional lands); nonland avg MV 2.954 -> 3.000; colored pips U23/B25/R22 -> U27/B25/R20. Hypergeometric (99-card library, no mulligans): P(2-5 lands in opening 7) 0.758 -> 0.741; P(>=4 lands in top 10) 0.470 -> 0.441; P(>=4 of lands+rocks in top 10) 0.687 -> 0.662. Cutting the tapped tri-land is a deliberate ~3-point land-drop trade for a spell slot, not a free change; the full-100 alternative that keeps 34 lands and cuts Talisman of Indulgence instead was built and rejected because the rock is the turn-4 Brass accelerant.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Stack: Counterspell, Mana Drain, Fierce Guardianship, Deflecting Swat, Siren Stormtamer; removal: Chaos Warp, Cyclonic Rift, Deadly Rollick, Feed the Swarm, Hostage Taker, Amphin Mutineer, Merchant Raiders channel, Otawara, Toxic Deluge; adds Kitesail Larcenist (one permanent per opponent, repeatable via Brass), Warkite Marauder (per-attack neutralization) and Siren's Ruse (instant-speed save + Pirate draw). Graveyard hate (Bojuka Bog, Rest in Peace) is the main weakness; the list keeps castable Pirates, Kindred Discovery and Breeches/Ramirez card flow as a non-graveyard plan.

weakest_slots.weakness: Two-mana conditional Treasure only on turns we descended; as a Brass return it is a vanilla 4/4 haste with a weak end-step clause.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Lowest-impact Pirate: no ETB, no attack trigger, no protection; ramp role is duplicated by Lannery, Corsair Captain, Gemcutter, Malcolm Navigator, Ramirez and Black Market Connections.

weakest_slots.weakness: Can't block; explore only on Pirate damage; a 2-drop evasive body with marginal value as a Brass target.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Explore is small card selection; the slot is better spent on a two-drop that converts Brass's haste into an extra turn (another Brass trigger).

weakest_slots.weakness: Attack trigger costs {2} for a 2/2 token and needs another nontoken Pirate; mana-hungry and slow in multiplayer.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Same mana slot; Warkite's free attack trigger neutralizes the best blocker every combat and doubles under Roaming Throne.

weakest_slots.weakness: 1-drop that cannot block; its only text is evasion.
weakest_slots.reasoning: REV2 (after ChatGPT review): RETAINED. As a Brass return it is a hasty 4/4 that can't be blocked, so it reliably connects. That counts toward Admiral Beckett Brass's three-Pirate theft condition and triggers Breeches, Brazen Plunderer, Ramirez and Shared Animosity. Ragavan's Treasure and card need combat damage that blockers can deny (RETAIN_ALTERNATIVE).

weakest_slots.weakness: No Treasure for Brass-returned Pirates while their finality counter is on, since they are exiled instead of dying. It still triggers on other deaths: hard-cast creatures, tokens (Amphin encore copies), Victimize/Bombardiers sacrifices of non-finality creatures, stolen creatures we control, Pirates whose counter Power Conduit removed (or blinked by Siren's Ruse), and our side of Toxic Deluge / Living Death.
weakest_slots.reasoning: REV2 recheck: Plunderer is not globally switched off. Its payable cases are real but mostly incidental (roughly 0-2 Treasures in a typical turn cycle; bursts only on our own sweepers). Jhoira returned by Brass is a hasty 4/4 that steals two historic permanents the turn it arrives (ETB + attack; four with Roaming Throne), for life equal to their MV. Jhoira's ceiling is higher and the swap stays, at MODERATE confidence.

weakest_slots.weakness: Always-tapped tri-land; the 34th physical land (34 land cards in 31 rows: Island/Mountain/Swamp x2) alongside 8 rocks and many Treasure makers.
weakest_slots.reasoning: REV2: CUT for Siren's Ruse. Corrected count: 34 lands + 8 rocks = 42 mana permanents plus Brass's Tunnel-Grinder (an artifact on the front face, not a playable land). 33 lands cost about 3 points of land-drop probability (P(>=4 lands in 10 cards) 0.470 -> 0.441). The tapped land is the least valuable one. Nesting Grounds (colorless, sorcery speed) remains a non-selected alternative.

weakest_slots.weakness: Third two-mana BR rock in an eight-rock suite; low ceiling after turn three.
weakest_slots.reasoning: A free sacrifice outlet only pays off with stolen creatures or counter-removed Pirates; the rock is the more reliable commander-on-curve card (REJECT).

weakest_slots.weakness: Three-mana lord + one Treasure; as a Brass return its anthem does not include itself.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Ravager's symmetric one-third life loss also hits this life-paying deck (shocks, Talismans, BMC, Vampiric, Reanimate, Confluence); lord + mana is steadier (REJECT).

weakest_slots.weakness: Five-mana; Vehicle clause nearly blank (only The Indomitable); value is end-step Treasures from tapped Pirates.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Crew's threaten activation costs {3}{R} per use and lacks a free sac outlet; Kenway's Treasure output after an alpha strike is larger (REJECT).

weakest_slots.weakness: Four-mana; value depends on a stream of Pirate entries.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Raiders locks a blocker on every Brass return (each return is a Pirate entering) and channels as removal; Copy is a clone whose value depends on the board (REJECT).

weakest_slots.weakness: Symmetric: every opponent returns their own chosen type.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Back in Town is one-sided but X-costed and returns only outlaws for {X}{2}{B}; Bidding returns all Pirates for five and also hits changeling tokens; retained.

weakest_slots.weakness: Card disadvantage; its value is only discarding Pirates for Brass.
weakest_slots.reasoning: REV2: CUT for Ripples of Undeath. It is a one-shot -2 cards, while Ripples mills 3 every turn in the first main phase, before Brass's beginning-of-combat trigger chooses a target, and can buy one milled card for {1} and 3 life. Big Score and Windfall were rejected earlier against this slot.

weakest_slots.weakness: Two-mana artifact that does nothing alone.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Conduit is instant-speed and not a creature (no summoning-sickness delay), so the finality counter can be removed the same combat the Pirate returns; Diviner needs a full turn cycle and dies to sweepers; retained.

weakest_slots.weakness: Boast sacrifice only once per turn and only after attacking.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Bombardiers is a sac outlet that converts the sacrificed permanent into 2+MV damage; Pit is a free outlet that does nothing alone; retained.

whole_deck_audit.current_baseline_strength: The approved Oct 13 list is coherent and already strong: it fixed the older Proposed_Final by adding Mary Read and Anne Bonny, Brass's Tunnel-Grinder and Power Conduit and dropping Windfall/Ghost of Ramirez. Its weakness is a handful of low-ceiling two-drop Pirates and one death-trigger card that the finality counter disables.
whole_deck_audit.candidate_pool_scope: Historical pool (Soul Diviner, Grim Captain's Locker, Back in Town, Arm-Mounted Anchor, Port of Karfell, Nephalia Drownyard, Warkite Marauder, Kitesail Larcenist, Dire Fleet Ravager, Nesting Grounds); EDHREC all-decks and optimized commander pages (2026-10-23); a full frozen-cache Oracle scan of 140 commander-legal UBR Pirate creatures not in the list; plus a targeted scan for free sacrifice outlets, counter movers, extra combats and all-types enablers.
whole_deck_audit.off_ranked_search_conclusion: OFF-RANKING search found Jhoira, Weatherlight Corsair (EDHREC New Cards only, 6/21 optimized decks) — selected — and confirmed Ashnod's Altar, Spawning Pit, Maskwood Nexus and Karlach as plausible but rejected. Nephalia Drownyard was not material (colorless slow mill competes with a colored land slot).

final_changes.coherent_package_tradeoff: REV2 six one-for-one swaps (rev1 five-swap list superseded; kept as history). Four Pirate-for-Pirate upgrades replace low-ceiling Pirates with Pirates whose ETB or attack triggers Brass multiplies: repeatable multiplayer removal (Larcenist), per-attack blocker neutralization (Warkite), extra turns from a hasty return (Navigator), a premium two-steal reanimation target (Jhoira). Two non-Pirate swaps added after ChatGPT's review: Siren's Ruse for the 34th land (finality reset, ETB retrigger, protection, Pirate draw) and Ripples of Undeath for Faithless Looting (repeatable precombat mill before Brass's combat trigger). Pirate count unchanged (28 in the 99 by quantity, counting Changeling Outcast; 29 with the commander). Lands 34 -> 33 with 8 rocks kept; avg nonland MV 2.954 -> 3.000. Lost roles: conditional Treasure/explore/2-2 tokens, Plunderer's incidental death Treasure, one tapped tri-land and a one-shot looter. Changeling Outcast is kept: the rev1 Ragavan swap is reverted.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Two-mana conditional Treasure only on turns we descended; as a Brass return it is a vanilla 4/4 haste with a weak end-step clause.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Lowest-impact Pirate: no ETB, no attack trigger, no protection; ramp role is duplicated by Lannery, Corsair Captain, Gemcutter, Malcolm Navigator, Ramirez and Black Market Connections.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Can't block; explore only on Pirate damage; a 2-drop evasive body with marginal value as a Brass target.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Explore is small card selection; the slot is better spent on a two-drop that converts Brass's haste into an extra turn (another Brass trigger).

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Attack trigger costs {2} for a 2/2 token and needs another nontoken Pirate; mana-hungry and slow in multiplayer.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Same mana slot; Warkite's free attack trigger neutralizes the best blocker every combat and doubles under Roaming Throne.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: 1-drop that cannot block; its only text is evasion.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: REV2 (after ChatGPT review): RETAINED. As a Brass return it is a hasty 4/4 that can't be blocked, so it reliably connects. That counts toward Admiral Beckett Brass's three-Pirate theft condition and triggers Breeches, Brazen Plunderer, Ramirez and Shared Animosity. Ragavan's Treasure and card need combat damage that blockers can deny (RETAIN_ALTERNATIVE).

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: No Treasure for Brass-returned Pirates while their finality counter is on, since they are exiled instead of dying. It still triggers on other deaths: hard-cast creatures, tokens (Amphin encore copies), Victimize/Bombardiers sacrifices of non-finality creatures, stolen creatures we control, Pirates whose counter Power Conduit removed (or blinked by Siren's Ruse), and our side of Toxic Deluge / Living Death.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: REV2 recheck: Plunderer is not globally switched off. Its payable cases are real but mostly incidental (roughly 0-2 Treasures in a typical turn cycle; bursts only on our own sweepers). Jhoira returned by Brass is a hasty 4/4 that steals two historic permanents the turn it arrives (ETB + attack; four with Roaming Throne), for life equal to their MV. Jhoira's ceiling is higher and the swap stays, at MODERATE confidence.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Always-tapped tri-land; the 34th physical land (34 land cards in 31 rows: Island/Mountain/Swamp x2) alongside 8 rocks and many Treasure makers.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: REV2: CUT for Siren's Ruse. Corrected count: 34 lands + 8 rocks = 42 mana permanents plus Brass's Tunnel-Grinder (an artifact on the front face, not a playable land). 33 lands cost about 3 points of land-drop probability (P(>=4 lands in 10 cards) 0.470 -> 0.441). The tapped land is the least valuable one. Nesting Grounds (colorless, sorcery speed) remains a non-selected alternative.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Third two-mana BR rock in an eight-rock suite; low ceiling after turn three.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: A free sacrifice outlet only pays off with stolen creatures or counter-removed Pirates; the rock is the more reliable commander-on-curve card (REJECT).

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Three-mana lord + one Treasure; as a Brass return its anthem does not include itself.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Ravager's symmetric one-third life loss also hits this life-paying deck (shocks, Talismans, BMC, Vampiric, Reanimate, Confluence); lord + mana is steadier (REJECT).

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Five-mana; Vehicle clause nearly blank (only The Indomitable); value is end-step Treasures from tapped Pirates.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Crew's threaten activation costs {3}{R} per use and lacks a free sac outlet; Kenway's Treasure output after an alpha strike is larger (REJECT).

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Four-mana; value depends on a stream of Pirate entries.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Raiders locks a blocker on every Brass return (each return is a Pirate entering) and channels as removal; Copy is a clone whose value depends on the board (REJECT).

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Symmetric: every opponent returns their own chosen type.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Back in Town is one-sided but X-costed and returns only outlaws for {X}{2}{B}; Bidding returns all Pirates for five and also hits changeling tokens; retained.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Card disadvantage; its value is only discarding Pirates for Brass.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: REV2: CUT for Ripples of Undeath. It is a one-shot -2 cards, while Ripples mills 3 every turn in the first main phase, before Brass's beginning-of-combat trigger chooses a target, and can buy one milled card for {1} and 3 life. Big Score and Windfall were rejected earlier against this slot.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Two-mana artifact that does nothing alone.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Conduit is instant-speed and not a creature (no summoning-sickness delay), so the finality counter can be removed the same combat the Pirate returns; Diviner needs a full turn cycle and dies to sweepers; retained.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Boast sacrifice only once per turn and only after attacking.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Bombardiers is a sac outlet that converts the sacrificed permanent into 2+MV damage; Pit is a free outlet that does nothing alone; retained.

multi_slot_packages.result_and_rationale: Selected REV2 six-swap package; every add is independently justified, Pirate density is preserved and the mana base is one land lighter (34 -> 33) with the trade quantified in the mana audit.

Tempo/setup package on top of REV2 (each also built as its own seven-swap full-100). Prismari rejected: loses the creature/enchantment answer. Ragavan (rev1's selected swap) re-tested and Reverted: a Brass-returned Outcast is an unblockable hasty 4/4 that always connects for Beckett/Breeches/Ramirez/Shared Animosity; Ragavan's payoff needs unblocked damage.
Counter-movement + free sacrifice loop package: re-use one best ETB Pirate every turn. Rejected — two-card dependency and colorless land fixing loss.
Aggression/steal package. Rejected — self-damage, mana-costed threaten redundant with Coercive Recruiter, and Spawning Pit is the weakest outlet.

low_swap_heightened_audit.alternate_cuts_for_prior_holds: Prior holds re-examined: Power Conduit (kept over Soul Diviner for timing), Patriarch's Bidding (kept over Back in Town), Faithless Looting (kept over Big Score/Windfall in rev1; REV2 cuts it for Ripples of Undeath), Feed the Swarm (kept over Prismari Command), Changeling Outcast (kept over Ragavan; rev1 reversal), Merchant Raiders (kept over Dire Fleet Ravager — reverses my earlier Pass C advisory).
low_swap_heightened_audit.strongest_argument_against_baseline: Scallywag, Francisco and Fathom Fleet Captain do almost nothing extra when Brass returns them, yet returning Pirates is the commander's whole engine. Pitiless Plunderer produces nothing from Brass-returned Pirates while their finality counter is on, though it still pays off on other deaths. The baseline also runs a heavy 34 lands + 8 rocks, and it lacks a cheap instant reset/protection and a repeatable precombat self-mill.
low_swap_heightened_audit.evidence_based_answer: Replace those four with Pirates whose triggers scale with Brass and Roaming Throne, and convert the 34th land and the one-shot looter into Siren's Ruse and Ripples of Undeath. Changeling Outcast stays because its guaranteed connection matters. Earlier wording proposed replacing five with Pirates whose triggers scale with Brass and Roaming Throne. Prevalence figures (EDHREC) are discovery evidence only; the decision rests on Oracle text, rulings and role audit, not on win rates (none measured).

open_ended_optimization_audit.remaining_99_review: REV2 (after ChatGPT review) re-challenged the remaining slots: lands (34 by quantity; the tapped tri-land Crumbling Necropolis now cut; Xander's Lounge kept because it is fetchable and cycles; Nesting Grounds/Port of Karfell rejected), rocks (Talismans/Signets vs Ashnod's Altar, Spawning Pit, Herald's Horn, and Talisman of Indulgence vs Siren's Ruse as the 34-land alternative), Pirates (Changeling Outcast vs Ragavan, re-reversed; Corsair Captain vs Dire Fleet Ravager; Edward Kenway vs Captivating Crew/Karlach; Merchant Raiders vs Pirated Copy; Siren Stormtamer vs Spectral Sailor), spells (Faithless Looting -> Ripples of Undeath; Feed the Swarm vs Prismari Command; Deflecting Swat vs Ghostly Flicker; Patriarch's Bidding vs Back in Town), engines (Power Conduit vs Soul Diviner, Kindred Discovery vs Maskwood Nexus, Lightning Greaves vs Grim Captain's Locker).

post_floor_challenges.tradeoff: REV2 SELF-CHALLENGE #1 (ChatGPT item 3b). Ragavan is a Monkey Pirate (verified). When Brass returns either card, Outcast is a hasty 4/4 that can't be blocked and always connects, which counts toward Beckett's three-Pirate theft condition and triggers Breeches, Brazen Plunderer, Ramirez and Shared Animosity. Ragavan is a blockable 4/4 whose Treasure and card need that same connection. Ragavan's one-drop hard-cast tempo is real but not decisive in four-player pods with blockers. Seven-swap file built; kept as an alternative.

REV2 SELF-CHALLENGE #2 (ChatGPT item 2). The instant loot-two plus Treasure is good precombat setup, but Feed the Swarm is the list's cheap answer to any creature or enchantment. Prismari answers only artifacts or two-toughness creatures and adds a blue pip on top of a +4 blue-pip shift. Seven-swap file built; rejected.

The Altar nets mana only by sacrificing creatures. A Brass-returned Pirate is exiled by finality unless Conduit or Siren's Ruse reset it first. Plunderer is cut, so there is no Treasure loop, and Bombardiers/Victimize already supply outlets. Talisman is a turn-2 B/R source toward turn-4 Brass. REJECT.

Brief scan of instant blink: two blinks reset two finality counters and retrigger ETBs, but it costs three and draws no card. Siren's Ruse already fills the role, and Swat is free protection with Brass out.
Symmetric one-third life loss also taxes our own life-paying mana and tutors (and Ripples' life payment); the lord+Treasure three-drop is steadier.
Mana-costed sorcery threaten duplicates Coercive Recruiter's free steals; Kenway's end-step Treasures fund recasts.
Pit needs Power Conduit or a stolen creature to matter and makes no mana; sacrificing a finality Pirate exiles it.

larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Gives up the cheap catch-all creature/enchantment removal; Ripples already supplies precombat graveyard setup. Not clearly better than the incumbent.

open_ended_optimization_audit.quality_based_stop_reason: REV2 stop after ChatGPT review: six swaps, not because of any count target. Two outside candidates the review raised (Siren's Ruse, Ripples of Undeath) beat specific incumbents (the 34th land, Faithless Looting) and were added. The next-best outsiders lose concretely as full-100 files: Ragavan vs Changeling Outcast (guaranteed connection), Prismari Command vs Feed the Swarm (enchantment/creature answer), plus Nesting Grounds, Ashnod's Altar, Ghostly Flicker, Spectral Sailor, Dire Fleet Ravager, Captivating Crew and Spawning Pit. The rev1 self-challenge on Nesting Grounds and Ashnod's Altar still holds with corrected numbers (Nesting Grounds costs one source of each color, sorcery speed only; Altar is conditional), and both stay out. Adding further cards would be padding, not improvement. No global-optimality claim.
